newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares edge higher in narrow trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares edge higher in narrow trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares moved in narrow price ranges on Friday in subdued and cautious trade ahead of the weekend, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,570, up five points, or 0.32 percent, from Thursday after moving in a tight range between 1,556 and 1,584. Trade volume firmed to 19.24 trillion lira from Thursday's 18.92 trillion.
Over the week, the index gained 1.2 percent after last week's 6.2 percent loss caused by political concerns.

"The market was again overshadowed by politics this week mainly due to reported tension within the coalition government, although we were hoping that such worries would subside after last week's fall," said Soner Canoglu from Yatirim Investment.
"The index seems to have firm support at around the 1,500 mark, so it may recover next week. If the 1,650 resistance can be pierced with strong volume, the rise will continue," he said.
Brokers said lower trade volumes seen this week were partly due to income tax payments, adding that a liquidity drain ahead of a 4-1/2-day holiday from April 17 to April 22 was also awaited.
They said March inflation data came out in line with the expectations and thus did not have any effect.

Turkey's wholesale prices rose 6.0 percent month-on-month in March after a rise of 6.2 percent in February and consumer prices rose 5.4 percent, compared with a rise of 5.7 percent the previous month.

Of the 242 shares traded, 93 advanced, 71 declined and 78 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial firmed 0.45 percent to 1,568, the IMKB Services rose 1.39 percent to 1,463 and the IMKB Financial eased 0.12 percent to 1,682.

Leading actives were automotive firm Otosan, up 2,000 lira at 80,000, Ihlas Holding, up 1,500 lira at 27,000 and utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 220,000. They made up 28.7 percent of the total turnover.
